recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. No FHIR core follow-up is recommended for FHIR-16097 unless the work group wants new guidance for the Extension Pack processing/manipulation extensions or a new current-core modeling rule.
issue_request: FHIR-16097 was Published/Persuasive for BiologicallyDerivedProduct and asked for an example use case clarifying the distinction between processing and manipulation. The decisive Jira comment distinguishes non-altering processing, such as adding anti-coagulants during PBSC collection, from manipulation intended to alter the product, such as buffy-coat enrichment or CD8 reduction.
initial_application: Jira cites commit b4bd0b1, which updated the then-active BiologicallyDerivedProduct spreadsheet definitions for .processing and .manipulation with the requested explanatory examples.
additional_context: Later Published/Persuasive-with-Modification issue FHIR-33068 replaced the BDP attribute set for R5. Commit a261b7c666 removed the old core .processing and .manipulation backbone elements while adding generic property support. The old processing/manipulation concepts now exist as FHIR Extension Pack definitions, where the FHIR-16097 clarifying examples remain present.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current core StructureDefinition is active and lists processingFacility, collection, and property but no separate .processing or .manipulation elements; adding the old use-case prose back to core would describe removed core elements or duplicate correct Extension Pack definitions.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 replacement of the BiologicallyDerivedProduct attribute set removed the old core processing/manipulation elements and introduced generic property support, changing how FHIR-16097 applies to current core.
